questions.prompt: A visitor says they are a device representative and asks to observe an operation. What should the circulating nurse verify first?
options: Permission to enter the surgical suite
Whether the surgeon has used that device before
questions.explanation: The CNA competency includes verifying authorization for visitors, including industry representatives.

questions.prompt: A patient asks that a family member not hear details of the procedure. What should guide the handoff?
options: Protect the patient's confidentiality while sharing necessary care information
Tell every family member because surgery is high risk
Omit the information from all team handoffs
Ask the visitor to decide what may be shared
questions.explanation: Advocacy includes privacy and confidentiality, while care transitions still require relevant clinical information.

questions.prompt: A nurse notices a break in sterile technique that no one else has seen. Which action best reflects surgical conscience?
options: Speak up and correct the break
Wait until the wound is closed
Document it without interrupting the case
Assume the scrub person will notice
questions.explanation: Surgical conscience calls for acting on an observed risk even when unnoticed.

questions.prompt: A patient has limited English proficiency during preoperative teaching. What is the best response?
options: Arrange effective language support and check understanding
Ask the accompanying child to interpret complex consent
questions.explanation: The blueprint requires addressing communication needs, including language barriers.

questions.prompt: Which record best meets the blueprint's documentation competency?
options: A timely account of count results, positioning, medications, specimens and key events
A summary written several days later from memory
A note limited to incision and closing times
questions.explanation: Documentation should be complete, accurate and contemporaneous.

questions.prompt: During transfer to recovery, what is the perioperative nurse's priority communication task?
options: Give a structured handoff of relevant care and accountability
Send the chart without verbal communication
Wait for the next shift to relay concerns
questions.explanation: CNA identifies communication and accountability at care transitions.

questions.prompt: A patient expresses fear about altered body image after surgery. Which response fits perioperative advocacy?
options: Acknowledge the concern and incorporate psychosocial support
Reassure them that appearance is unimportant
Avoid the topic because it is postoperative
Ask the patient to discuss it only with family
questions.explanation: The competency explicitly includes psychosocial needs such as altered body image.

questions.prompt: A colleague makes a demeaning remark during a case. What is the best professional response?
options: Address and report the behaviour through appropriate processes
Ignore it because the patient is anesthetized
Post about it on social media
Retaliate in front of the team
questions.explanation: The blueprint includes a respectful workplace and reporting unprofessional behaviour.

questions.prompt: A new technology is introduced in the OR. What is the nurse's safest starting point?
options: Identify learning needs and obtain training before independent use
Let a vendor direct nursing care
questions.explanation: CNA identifies adaptation to technology and continuing learning within scope.

questions.prompt: A surgeon asks a nurse to perform a task outside their authorized scope. What should the nurse do?
options: Clarify the request and remain within applicable scope and competence
Perform it if the surgeon insists
Ask a student to do it
Document it as a routine nursing task
questions.explanation: Scope is governed by provincial or territorial licensure and competence.

questions.prompt: A wrong-site procedure is narrowly prevented before incision. What is the nurse's next professional obligation?
options: Report and document the event under the organization's process
Erase the schedule error because no injury occurred
Tell only the patient after discharge
Wait until the next month to review it
questions.explanation: The blueprint includes recognizing and reporting situations requiring disclosure.

questions.prompt: A patient has a specific spiritual practice relevant to their perioperative care. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Ask about and accommodate the practice where safe and feasible
Assume every member of that community wants the same accommodation
Dismiss it because surgical workflow takes priority
Ask family to speak for a capable patient
questions.explanation: Care should respond to individual beliefs without stereotypes.

questions.prompt: A team disagreement is escalating beside an awake patient. What should the nurse prioritize?
options: De-escalate and move conflict away from the patient
Continue the argument until one side yields
Record the interaction instead of intervening
Ask the patient to choose a side
questions.explanation: Conflict resolution includes de-escalation and separating parties.

questions.prompt: A research specimen is requested during surgery. What must be checked in addition to routine specimen handling?
options: The applicable research consent and approved protocol
Only whether the container is large enough
Whether the surgeon prefers fresh tissue
Whether a visitor can take it to the laboratory
questions.explanation: Research participation must follow consent and ethics-approved protocols.

questions.prompt: Which activity is a quality-improvement example named in the CNA blueprint?
options: Reviewing surgical site infection prevention performance
Changing a patient's consent without discussion
Delegating all counts to a vendor
Disabling incident reporting to reduce paperwork
questions.explanation: CNA cites SSI prevention, wound classification and checklist use as quality-improvement areas.

questions.prompt: What is the best educational approach when a patient asks about immediate postoperative expectations?
options: Give individualized teaching appropriate to the phase of care
Promise there will be no pain
Provide the same script regardless of procedure
questions.explanation: The blueprint includes education before, during and immediately after surgery.

questions.prompt: A competent patient requests privacy while being positioned. What should the team do?
options: Limit exposure and protect dignity throughout positioning
Discuss the patient in a public hallway
questions.explanation: Privacy and dignity remain nursing responsibilities throughout the perioperative period.

questions.prompt: A vendor offers to operate a surgical device on the patient. Which question is most important for the nurse?
options: Is that activity authorized within the individual's role and facility policy?
Has the vendor sold many devices?
Would the task save several minutes?
questions.explanation: Visitor permission and professional scope must both be respected.

questions.prompt: Which issue should be included in a recovery handoff after a difficult positioning case?
options: Areas of skin concern and positioning related risks
Only the number of staff in the room
questions.explanation: Relevant care findings must follow the patient through transition.

questions.prompt: A staff member discovers their charting has an error. What is the safest action?
options: Correct it using the record's approved amendment process
Ask another nurse to chart in their name
Leave it unchanged because the case is finished
questions.explanation: Accurate contemporaneous documentation includes transparent correction.

questions.prompt: At which point does the WHO checklist's Sign In occur?
questions.explanation: The WHO checklist separates Sign In, Time Out and Sign Out by phase.

questions.prompt: What is confirmed with the patient during Sign In?
questions.explanation: The WHO Sign In asks for patient confirmation of identity, site, procedure and consent.

questions.prompt: What equipment check belongs to Sign In?
questions.explanation: The anesthesia equipment and medication check is a Sign In item.

questions.prompt: What monitoring item is checked before induction on the WHO checklist?

questions.prompt: The WHO checklist flags anticipated major blood loss in an adult above what amount?
questions.explanation: The WHO Sign In threshold is more than 500 mL for adults.

questions.prompt: For a child, the WHO checklist flags expected blood loss above what threshold?
questions.explanation: The pediatric Sign In threshold is more than 7 mL/kg.

questions.prompt: When the checklist identifies a difficult airway or aspiration risk, what should also be confirmed?
questions.explanation: WHO pairs the risk with a plan for equipment and help.

questions.prompt: When is the WHO Time Out performed?
options: After the patient leaves the OR
questions.explanation: Time Out precedes incision.

questions.prompt: Who participates in the WHO Time Out?
questions.explanation: The checklist calls for the operative team to confirm together.

questions.prompt: Which identification is spoken during Time Out?
options: Patient name, procedure and incision site
questions.explanation: The team verbally confirms patient, procedure and site.

questions.prompt: What is the WHO prophylactic antibiotic prompt at Time Out?
options: Was it given within the preceding 60 minutes, if applicable?
Was it prescribed for 30 days after discharge?
Was it given only after closure?
Was it omitted for every case?
questions.explanation: The WHO checklist asks whether prophylaxis was given in the preceding 60 minutes.

questions.prompt: Which surgeon concern is explicitly discussed at Time Out?
options: Critical or nonroutine steps, case length and expected blood loss
Only the name of the instrument vendor
questions.explanation: Anticipated critical events are shared before incision.

questions.prompt: Which nursing concern is explicitly discussed at Time Out?
options: Sterility including indicator results and equipment issues
questions.explanation: The checklist prompts nursing review of sterility and equipment concerns.

questions.prompt: When is essential imaging confirmed to be displayed?
options: At Time Out before incision, when applicable
Only when the patient requests it
questions.explanation: Essential imaging is a preincision checklist prompt.

questions.prompt: At what point is WHO Sign Out completed?
options: Before the patient leaves the operating room
questions.explanation: Sign Out precedes departure from the OR.

questions.prompt: Which count result is verbally confirmed at Sign Out?
options: Only the number of staff present
questions.explanation: The WHO Sign Out requires verbal confirmation of these counts.

questions.prompt: Which specimen action is part of Sign Out?
options: Read specimen labels aloud, including patient name
Leave labelling to the receiving unit alone
questions.explanation: WHO calls for verbal specimen label confirmation.

questions.prompt: Who discusses key recovery concerns at Sign Out?
questions.explanation: The three disciplines share recovery and management concerns.

questions.prompt: A sponge count is discrepant before closure. What is the safest immediate course?

Assume the previous count was correct
Close and search the room later
Change the recorded count to match the expected count

questions.prompt: A scrub nurse is permanently relieved midcase. What count-related step is expected?

Rely on the morning's initial count
Count only at the end of the shift
Avoid count documentation because the case is ongoing

questions.prompt: Which phase is specifically identified for a surgical count?
options: Before closure of a cavity or incision
questions.explanation: CNA lists initial, before closure and procedure completion counts.

questions.prompt: An emergency case starts without a count. What should occur?
options: Notify the surgeon and follow imaging and documentation processes
Record a normal count by default
Do nothing because emergencies are exempt
questions.explanation: The blueprint explicitly includes response when a count could not be performed.

questions.prompt: Why should small sponges be loaded on instruments when indicated?

To make them absorb less blood

questions.prompt: Which positioning factor should be assessed preoperatively?

questions.prompt: Which intraoperative factor raises pressure injury risk?

The name of the instrument set

questions.prompt: Who collaborates on the final patient position before surgery begins?

questions.explanation: CNA specifies collaboration on final positioning.

questions.prompt: A patient will be placed in lithotomy. What should guide device selection?
options: Patient assessment, anatomy, procedure and pressure risk
questions.explanation: Positioning devices must suit patient and procedure.

questions.prompt: Before moving an anesthetized patient from the OR table, what should be assessed?
options: Physiological status, skin and safe transfer requirements
Only whether the next case is ready
questions.explanation: CNA calls for system assessment and safe transfer.

options: Assess dispersive electrode site, adhesion and size
Place the pad over any metal implant by default
Leave the active electrode on drapes
questions.explanation: The blueprint names pad placement, adhesion, size and alarm response.

questions.prompt: What should be checked before using monopolar electrosurgery on a patient with an implanted pacemaker?
options: Compatibility and an appropriate device plan with the team
Whether a bipolar instrument is in another room
questions.explanation: Implantable electronic devices need specific electrosurgical consideration.

questions.prompt: What is a safe place for an inactive electrosurgical pencil?
options: On the drape under a towel
questions.explanation: CNA lists active electrode isolation as a safety principle.

questions.prompt: Why verify alcohol-based skin preparation dry time before electrosurgery?
options: To reduce ignition and fire risk
To increase the volume of prep solution
To eliminate the need for oxygen monitoring

questions.prompt: What is a relevant safety control for surgical plume?
options: Rely on surgical masks alone in every case
Disable local suction to reduce turbulence

questions.prompt: Which hazard class best fits bone cement vapour exposure?

questions.prompt: Which hazard class best fits workplace harassment?

questions.prompt: What does WHMIS chiefly support in the OR?

questions.prompt: When a pneumatic tourniquet is used, what should the team monitor?
options: Pressure and duration according to the plan
Only the colour of the cuff
Only the number of instruments opened
questions.explanation: CNA names limb occlusion pressure and duration.

questions.prompt: What is the safest response to an unanticipated laser case without eye protection ready?
options: Pause until the controlled-area precautions and correct protection are in place
Proceed because general eyewear is equivalent
Ask observers to close their eyes
Use the laser at lower power without precautions

questions.prompt: Which compressed gas related issue merits a safety check?
options: Secure and use the cylinder according to facility procedure
Ignore connections if the tank is full
Use any regulator that fits loosely
questions.explanation: Compressed gas is included among equipment safety competencies.

questions.prompt: A laparoscopic case may convert to open surgery. What should the circulating nurse anticipate?
options: Additional instruments and supplies for the changed approach
questions.explanation: The blueprint names conversion to open as an intraoperative event requiring adaptation.

questions.prompt: A surgical specimen is removed. Which chain of actions best supports safety?
options: Verify identity, label, document and send to the right destination
Use the incision site instead of patient identifiers
Let it leave the room without a handoff
questions.explanation: CNA identifies verification, labelling, documentation and delivery.

questions.prompt: A specimen must remain fresh for a specific test. What should the nurse do?
options: Confirm preservation instructions before placing it in fixative
questions.explanation: Fresh versus fixed preservation is an explicit specimen competency.

questions.prompt: Which medication practice is part of the perioperative safety domain?
options: Verify, label, administer and document medications appropriately
Leave unlabeled syringes on the field
Assume every clear solution is saline
Chart drugs before they are given
questions.explanation: The blueprint includes preparation, verification, labelling, delivery and documentation.

questions.prompt: Which three elements form the surgical fire triangle?
questions.explanation: OR fire prevention manages all three parts of the fire triangle.

questions.prompt: Which item can be a fuel during an operating room fire?
options: Patient consent form in the chart
questions.explanation: Alcohol preparations and drapes are examples of fuel.

questions.prompt: Which item is a potential ignition source near oxygen-enriched drapes?
questions.explanation: Electrosurgery can ignite nearby fuel in an oxygen-enriched environment.

questions.prompt: During a high-risk head and neck case, what should the team discuss before incision?
options: How to reduce the combined oxygen, ignition and fuel risk
questions.explanation: A fire risk briefing coordinates control of the fire triangle.

questions.prompt: A reusable surgical instrument enters sterile tissue. How is it classified?
questions.explanation: Critical items enter tissue or the vascular system and require sterilization.

questions.prompt: A device contacts a mucous membrane but does not enter sterile tissue. What is the minimum broad processing category?
options: High-level disinfection for a semicritical item
Sterilization of the room air only
questions.explanation: Semicritical items require at least high-level disinfection, subject to device instructions.

questions.prompt: A blood pressure cuff contacts intact skin. Which Spaulding class best fits?
options: Semicritical because it has a cuff
questions.explanation: Noncritical items contact intact skin.

questions.prompt: Which processing method is generally preferred for a heat-stable critical instrument?
options: Steam sterilization according to the manufacturer's instructions
questions.explanation: Critical devices require sterilization; steam is appropriate when compatible.

questions.prompt: What must determine a device's sterilization cycle selection?
questions.explanation: Cycle parameters and compatibility are device and process specific.

questions.prompt: A sterile package is found wet after processing. What is the safe response?
options: Treat it as compromised and arrange reprocessing
Place it directly on the field
Dry it with a towel and use it
Use it if the external tape changed colour
questions.explanation: Package integrity and verified processing matter for an aseptic field.

questions.prompt: A chemical indicator has not reached its expected endpoint. What should happen?
options: Do not use the item; investigate processing
Use it because the wrapper is intact
Add a second indicator after opening
Soak it in antiseptic and proceed
questions.explanation: CNA includes chemical quality controls; an unsatisfactory result cannot be ignored.

questions.prompt: What does an external chemical process indicator chiefly show?
options: Exposure to a process, not proof of sterility
That the inside of a complex tray is sterile
questions.explanation: A colour change alone does not establish sterility.

questions.prompt: Which monitoring combination is used to evaluate sterilization?
options: Room lighting, noise and case time
Only visual inspection of the wrapper
questions.explanation: CDC recommends routine mechanical, chemical and biological monitoring.

questions.prompt: For a load with implantable devices, what extra monitoring and release practice is recommended when possible?
options: Use a biological indicator and quarantine until negative
Release immediately after external tape changes
Skip monitoring if the case is urgent
Use a patient pulse oximeter as the indicator
questions.explanation: CDC recommends a biological indicator for implant loads and quarantine when possible.

questions.prompt: An instrument falls below the sterile field. What should the team do?
options: Remove it from use and replace it with a verified sterile item
Return it to the tray if no one saw it
Rinse it with sterile saline and reuse it
questions.explanation: CNA requires recognizing and correcting breaks in asepsis.

questions.prompt: A scrubbed team member's gown is visibly contaminated. What is the appropriate response?
options: Correct the contamination, including regowning as needed
Avoid mentioning it to the team
questions.explanation: Compromised surgical attire requires corrective action.

questions.prompt: What practice maintains the sterile field during a procedure?
options: Continuous observation and prompt correction of breaks
Assuming every item placed on it is sterile
questions.explanation: CNA describes continuous surveillance of the sterile field.

questions.prompt: Before surgical hand antisepsis, what jewellery should be removed?

questions.prompt: What should be done to subungual debris before the surgical hand scrub?
options: Remove it with a nail cleaner under running water
Ignore it if the nails are short
Use alcohol only on the glove exterior
questions.explanation: CDC identifies cleaning under the nails before antisepsis.

questions.prompt: With antimicrobial soap, whose scrub duration should be followed?
options: A fixed ten minutes for every product
questions.explanation: CDC says follow the manufacturer, often 2 to 6 minutes.

questions.prompt: When using an alcohol-based surgical hand rub with persistent activity, when are sterile gloves donned?
options: After the hands and forearms are fully dry
While the product is still wet
Immediately after rinsing with tap water
questions.explanation: CDC advises allowing the product to dry before sterile gloves.

questions.prompt: Why is surgical hand antisepsis performed despite use of sterile gloves?
options: Gloves may tear or puncture during surgery
questions.explanation: Reducing hand flora limits contamination if a glove is compromised.

questions.prompt: When moving from a soiled site to a clean site on the same patient, what should happen?
options: Change gloves and perform hand hygiene as indicated
Keep the same gloves to save time
Use a second pair over the soiled gloves
questions.explanation: CDC lists site transition as an indication to change gloves and clean hands.

questions.prompt: If hair removal is needed at an incision site, what method is preferred?

questions.explanation: WHO recommends avoiding hair removal or clipping when necessary.

questions.prompt: Why can razor shaving increase surgical site infection risk?
options: It sterilizes the site too early
questions.explanation: Microscopic cuts from shaving can promote infection.

questions.prompt: What is the broad reason for maintaining normothermia during surgery?
options: Reduced hypothermia supports tissue perfusion and healing
It removes the need for skin prep
questions.explanation: WHO describes hypothermia reducing blood flow and slowing healing.

questions.prompt: For prophylaxis alone, what is the WHO position on extending antibiotics after surgery?
options: Routine postoperative continuation does not prevent SSI and may promote resistance
questions.explanation: WHO distinguishes prophylaxis before/during surgery from treatment of established infection.

questions.prompt: A patient has an airborne infection concern. What should planning include?
options: Additional airborne precautions and suitable traffic/environment measures
questions.explanation: The CNA blueprint includes routine practices plus airborne precautions.

questions.prompt: Which transmission category is listed for influenza in the CNA blueprint?

questions.prompt: Which transmission category is listed for multidrug-resistant organisms in the blueprint?

questions.prompt: Renovation near operating rooms may heighten which infection concern?

questions.prompt: Which set of measures is explicitly named for SSI reduction?

Uncovered on a clean supply cart
In a sterile tray for immediate reuse
Handed directly to the next scrub person
questions.explanation: The blueprint includes safe handling and transportation of contaminated instruments.

questions.prompt: When should immediate-use steam sterilization be considered?
options: An emergent need under a validated, documented process
As the routine way to make up for insufficient inventory
Whenever the room is behind schedule
questions.explanation: CNA limits IUSS to appropriate emergent conditions and process controls.

questions.prompt: What should be reviewed when a sterilizer quality-control result is abnormal?
options: Process parameters, indicators and affected load disposition
Only the colour of scrub clothing
questions.explanation: Quality controls are part of establishing the aseptic environment.

questions.prompt: Which environmental factors can affect sterility in the OR?
questions.explanation: The blueprint names these environmental factors.

questions.prompt: What should a team do if a sterile item touches a nonsterile surface during setup?
options: Remove or replace the contaminated item
Cover the contact point with tape
Use it after rubbing with dry gauze
questions.explanation: CNA requires corrective action after an aseptic break.

questions.prompt: Why verify the procedure's wound classification?
options: It supports accurate documentation and infection prevention surveillance
questions.explanation: CNA includes assessment and verification of wound classification.

questions.prompt: A glove tears during an invasive procedure. What should be done?
options: Replace it promptly and perform hand hygiene as indicated
Continue if no bleeding is visible
questions.explanation: Damaged gloves should be changed to restore barrier protection.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of preoperative bathing or showering in WHO SSI guidance?
questions.explanation: WHO includes patient bathing among SSI prevention measures.

questions.prompt: Which patient identifiers should be checked preoperatively?
questions.explanation: CNA lists two unique patient identifiers in preoperative assessment.

questions.prompt: A patient reports a new medication allergy in the holding area. What should happen?
options: Communicate it and update the plan before exposure
Wait for recovery to document it
Assume the chart is more reliable
questions.explanation: Allergies and abnormal findings must inform the team before anesthesia and surgery.

options: Stop progression and resolve the discrepancy with the team and patient as appropriate
Choose the side on the schedule
Ask the scrub nurse to guess
Proceed and correct the chart later
questions.explanation: Consent and surgical site verification are preoperative checks.

questions.prompt: Which item belongs in a preoperative assessment?
questions.explanation: Fasting is one of CNA's preoperative verification elements.

questions.prompt: A patient has an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator. What should the nurse do?
options: Communicate its presence for anesthesia and energy-device planning
Ignore it because it is internal
Remove it in the holding area
Assume it is compatible with all electrosurgery
questions.explanation: Implantable electronic devices are part of preoperative review.

questions.prompt: A patient reports herbal supplement use. Why is it relevant?

It never matters if prescribed drugs are listed
questions.explanation: CNA includes medications and herbal supplements in physiologic assessment.

questions.prompt: Which preoperative issue can affect airway management?

questions.prompt: A patient has limited neck movement. What should be communicated?

Only the patient's preference for music

questions.prompt: A patient is anxious before induction. What environmental action supports anesthesia care?
questions.explanation: CNA lists a supportive, quieter environment during general anesthesia.

questions.prompt: What does pulse oximetry measure noninvasively?
questions.explanation: The blueprint includes pulse oximetry among monitoring devices.

questions.prompt: Which monitoring method directly displays cardiac electrical activity?
questions.explanation: ECG is a noninvasive monitoring example in the blueprint.

questions.prompt: When an abnormal intraoperative monitor finding appears, what should the nurse do?
options: Communicate promptly with anesthesia and the team while responding within role
Silence the alarm and continue setup

questions.prompt: A planned regional anesthetic changes to general anesthesia. What is the nursing response?

Leave the room until induction ends

questions.prompt: Which patient group requires anesthesia considerations specifically named in the blueprint?

questions.explanation: The blueprint names pediatric, bariatric, geriatric and obstetric considerations.

questions.prompt: What should be assessed intraoperatively as the case progresses?

questions.prompt: Which assessment belongs at the end of a case before transfer?

questions.prompt: A patient has a possible need for blood products. When should this be identified?

questions.prompt: Which event is explicitly named among intraoperative urgent responses?

Assume the surgeon needs no help

questions.prompt: A case requires unfamiliar equipment. What should be arranged before use?
options: Training, appropriate personnel and functional checks
A vendor operating outside authorized role
questions.explanation: CNA includes safe equipment use, teaching and managing resources.

questions.prompt: Which resource issue affects patient safety during transfer?
options: Adequate staff and appropriate transfer devices
Only the length of the corridor
questions.explanation: The blueprint includes safe transfers and appropriate devices.

questions.prompt: A planned implant is not in stock. What should the nurse do?
options: Communicate the shortage early and verify an approved plan
Open a different implant without checking
Conceal the issue until the incision
questions.explanation: Anticipation and team communication are core resource practices.

questions.prompt: A new sterile package has damaged wrapping. What is the resource decision?
options: Obtain a package with intact, verified sterility
Tape the damage and open it
Use the contents if needed urgently
Place it near a warmer to repair it
questions.explanation: A compromised barrier cannot be assumed sterile.

questions.prompt: The OR is short of a necessary item for the next case. What is the best operational action?
options: Escalate and plan supply before the patient is committed to the procedure
Start the case and hope it arrives
Alter the documentation to show availability
questions.explanation: Anticipating needs and resolving shortages preserves safe care.

questions.prompt: Which consideration matters when selecting an instrument reprocessing method?
options: Device compatibility and validated manufacturer instructions
The fastest cycle regardless of device
questions.explanation: Resource decisions must fit safe processing and device instructions.

questions.prompt: A patient needs a specialized transfer surface after surgery. When should it be arranged?
options: Before transfer, based on the individualized plan
After the patient has been moved unsafely
At the next day's quality meeting
questions.explanation: Safe transfer is a planned resource need.

questions.prompt: Why track equipment problems at Sign Out?
options: So they can be addressed before future use and in follow-up
questions.explanation: WHO asks about equipment issues; CNA includes safe use and resource management.

questions.prompt: What should be done when a procedure's complexity increases unexpectedly?
options: Reassess staffing, equipment and supplies with the team
Proceed with the original resource plan regardless
questions.explanation: Resource management adapts to patient and procedural need.

questions.prompt: A patient develops signs concerning for malignant hyperthermia. What is the team response?
options: Activate the malignant hyperthermia protocol immediately
Wait for a temperature above 42°C before alerting anyone
Treat it as an isolated sterile-field problem
questions.explanation: CNA specifically names recognition and protocol-based response to malignant hyperthermia.

questions.prompt: An intraoperative dysrhythmia progresses to cardiac arrest. Which established process should guide the response?
options: The cardiac arrest or Code Blue protocol
questions.explanation: CNA identifies cardiac events and the cardiac arrest protocol.

questions.prompt: A patient has suspected disseminated intravascular coagulation. What is the safest nursing response?
options: Alert the team and support the applicable therapeutic protocol
Give an unverified blood product independently
Assume all surgical bleeding is expected
questions.explanation: DIC is named as an exceptional event requiring protocol-based management.

questions.prompt: Following an unexpected intraoperative death, what should guide the nurse's actions?
options: Hospital policy and required communication and documentation
Discard all records to protect privacy
questions.explanation: CNA includes expected or unexpected intraoperative death and hospital policy.

questions.prompt: A specimen may be medicolegal evidence. What is the priority?
options: Follow evidence collection, preservation and chain-of-custody guidance
Let an unverified visitor transport it
Alter its label after it leaves the room
questions.explanation: The exceptional-events competency includes gathering and preserving evidence.

questions.prompt: Which activity has additional regulatory and standards requirements in CNA's exceptional-events domain?
options: Organ and tissue procurement and transplantation
questions.explanation: The blueprint identifies transplantation under relevant Canadian regulations and standards.

questions.prompt: A request for organ procurement is received. What should be checked before proceeding?
options: The authorized pathway and applicable procurement and transplantation procedures
questions.explanation: CNA calls for compliance with applicable procurement and transplantation requirements.

questions.prompt: Why should a suspected malignant hyperthermia response be rehearsed by the OR team?
options: Rapid coordinated action depends on knowing the protocol and resources
Only the surgeon needs to know the protocol
The event can be resolved by documentation alone
questions.explanation: The blueprint expects recognition and response under the MH protocol.

questions.prompt: Two urgent cases need the same image intensifier. What should the charge nurse do?
options: Resolve competing priorities through team communication and clinical urgency
Allocate it to whoever asks loudest
Hide its location from one team
Assume both rooms can use it simultaneously
questions.explanation: CNA names competing equipment priorities as a resource conflict.

questions.prompt: Which set is explicitly within resource planning?
options: Staffing, equipment, implants, rooms, time and supplies
questions.explanation: The CNA resource domain lists these planning elements.

questions.prompt: Which practice aligns with the resource sustainability competency?
options: Reduce unnecessary waste and reuse or recycle where safe and allowed
Skip sterile processing to save energy
Open every tray before determining need
questions.explanation: CNA includes reduce, reuse and recycle while patient safety remains essential.

questions.prompt: A new device is offered for trial. What is a sound nursing contribution?
options: Participate in structured evaluation of safety, usability and outcomes
Accept marketing claims as the only evidence
Avoid reporting problems during the trial
questions.explanation: CNA includes product and equipment trial evaluation.

questions.prompt: A recurring delay is traced to missing instruments. What is the improvement response?
options: Identify the process cause and recommend a measurable change
Blame one staff member without review
Order every tray for every case
questions.explanation: CNA includes recognizing inefficiency and continuous quality improvement.

questions.prompt: The initial sponge count is correct. A cavity is being closed, but the closing count is short one sponge. What is the first safety response?
options: Pause closure, recount and notify the surgeon
Record the expected number as correct
Skip documentation because the initial count was correct
questions.explanation: CNA's discrepancy process includes recount and surgeon notification.

questions.prompt: The team cannot resolve the sponge discrepancy after recount. Which next action fits the blueprint?
options: Follow the imaging and documentation pathway
Accept the initial count as final
Replace the missing sponge with another counted sponge
questions.explanation: Imaging and documentation are part of discrepancy resolution.

questions.prompt: The count discrepancy is resolved, but the event affected care. How should it appear in the record?
options: Accurately and contemporaneously according to policy
Not at all because it was resolved
As a normal count without context
questions.explanation: Count events and actions belong in accurate documentation.

questions.prompt: At Sign Out, which statement should be verbally confirmed?
options: Instrument, sponge and needle count completion
Only the time of the next operation
questions.explanation: The WHO Sign Out requires count confirmation.

questions.prompt: In holding, the nurse finds that the patient's consent specifies left knee but the list says right knee. What is the priority?
options: Stop progression and reconcile site and consent
Follow the schedule because it was printed last
Ask the device representative to choose
questions.explanation: Preoperative verification includes consent and surgical site.

questions.prompt: Before anesthesia induction, which WHO Sign In confirmation involves the patient?
questions.explanation: These patient confirmations are in Sign In.

questions.prompt: After the discrepancy is resolved, what should the team verbally reconfirm just before incision?
options: Patient name, procedure and incision site
questions.explanation: The WHO Time Out repeats the critical patient and site confirmation.

questions.prompt: If the discrepancy revealed a system error that nearly led to wrong-site surgery, what should occur?
options: Report and review it through the appropriate process
Delete the erroneous schedule with no report
Discuss it only outside the hospital
Wait until the next credential renewal
questions.explanation: CNA names reporting situations requiring disclosure and quality improvement.

questions.prompt: A wrapped instrument set arrives with a torn barrier. What should the scrub team do?
options: Reject it and obtain verified sterile instruments
Open it because the tray looks clean
Place a sterile towel over the tear
questions.explanation: A compromised package cannot support an aseptic field.

questions.prompt: A replacement critical instrument is heat stable. Which processing category is required?
options: Sterilization, with steam when compatible and validated
No processing if it is new
questions.explanation: Critical instruments entering sterile tissue require sterilization.

questions.prompt: The internal chemical indicator suggests inadequate processing. What is the correct disposition?
options: Do not use the set; investigate and reprocess appropriately
Use it because the external tape changed
Repeat the colour check after the incision
Place the indicator beside the patient
questions.explanation: An unsatisfactory internal indicator means the set should not be used.

questions.prompt: The missing sterile set threatens case readiness. What should be coordinated?
options: A safe alternative, timing and team communication
Use the failed set without informing anyone
Move the patient before the equipment plan is resolved
questions.explanation: Resource planning must preserve the verified sterile supply.

questions.prompt: A head and neck case uses supplemental oxygen, alcohol prep and electrosurgery. Which combination creates fire risk?
options: Oxidizer, fuel and ignition source together
questions.explanation: Oxygen, prep and electrosurgery map to the fire triangle.

questions.prompt: Before electrosurgery near the prepared field, what check matters?
options: The alcohol prep has dried according to instructions
The oxygen flow is increased automatically
questions.explanation: Prep dry time and flammability are ESU safety considerations.

questions.prompt: Where should the inactive electrosurgical pencil be kept?
questions.explanation: Active-electrode isolation reduces inadvertent ignition or injury.

questions.prompt: The team identifies a near fire during setup. What is the best immediate action?
options: Pause and control oxygen, ignition and fuel hazards together
Ignore the concern after Time Out
questions.explanation: Fire prevention is coordinated control of the triangle.

questions.prompt: A bariatric patient is scheduled for a prolonged laparoscopic procedure. What should the preoperative plan include?
options: Individualized positioning and safe transfer equipment
No extra assessment if anesthesia is planned
questions.explanation: The blueprint addresses bariatric considerations and safe positioning and transfer.

questions.prompt: Which factor increases this patient's intraoperative pressure injury risk?
options: The printed date on the schedule
questions.explanation: Case duration and positioning devices are recognized risks.

questions.prompt: The laparoscopy converts to open surgery. What should the circulator anticipate?
options: Additional instruments, supplies and updated care plan
questions.explanation: CNA explicitly describes conversion requiring adaptation.

questions.prompt: Before transfer to recovery, what should be assessed and communicated?
options: Skin, thermoregulation, pain and transfer needs
Only the next case's start time
questions.explanation: Postoperative assessment and safe transfer needs follow the patient.

questions.prompt: During anesthesia a patient develops an unexpected severe dysrhythmia. What should guide the response?
options: Rapid team communication and the cardiac event protocol
Only the regular Sign Out checklist
questions.explanation: CNA names cardiac events and protocol-based response.

questions.prompt: The response needs extra personnel and emergency equipment. What should the circulator coordinate?
options: Staff, equipment and room resources by clinical priority
questions.explanation: Resource planning includes staffing and equipment availability.

questions.prompt: Once stabilized, how should the event be handed off?
options: Provide a structured account of what happened and ongoing concerns
Say only that surgery is over
Leave the receiving team to discover it in the chart
Wait for a family member to explain it
questions.explanation: Care transitions require relevant information and accountability.

questions.prompt: What should be entered in the nursing record?
options: The event, interventions and relevant times accurately
questions.explanation: Complete, contemporaneous event documentation supports continuity.

cases.C1: During an abdominal operation, the initial count is correct. The team is preparing to close a body cavity.
cases.C2: An adult patient arrives in holding for a unilateral knee operation. The consent and schedule disagree about the side.
cases.C3: A patient is scheduled for surgery requiring a heat-stable critical instrument. A wrapped set arrives with a damaged barrier.
cases.C4: A head and neck case uses supplemental oxygen, alcohol-based skin preparation and an electrosurgical pencil.
cases.C5: A bariatric patient is scheduled for a prolonged laparoscopic procedure that may require conversion to an open approach.
cases.C6: A patient develops a severe unexpected dysrhythmia during an operation and needs an urgent team response.
